REVIEW a71a3ad9c5fb4e5176c7e526a859b8e2d5e9e965 (lexical, bd-01M381YHAXMH9F5HZD8P7DKTBX): APPROVE. No BLOCK.
- Semantics are unchanged. The old SemanticDistance.of(f) was exactly Estimate.observed(f(u, n)), so the new SAM (unit, node) => ContentLexical.score(...) is the same value, and the both-empty case is still 1.0.
- Independent run, fresh --shared clone at the exact SHA, with fatal warnings: ContentLexicalSuite plus ContradictionParityPin, 5/0.
- Mutant L1 (both-empty gives 0.0) and mutant L2 (denominator |a|+|b| instead of the union) are each killed by "the historical provider preserves the pinned Jaccard grid". Source restored, tree clean. Logs: ~/.claude/jobs/48a9214c/tmp/lx-*.log.
FOLLOW-UPs (not blocking):
F1. The test "typed lexical scoring agrees with the historical provider" is now tautological, because lexicalJaccard IS ContentLexical.score on sourceUnit/sourceNode. It cannot fail independently. The literal grid is the real witness. Either drop it or keep it labelled as a regression guard.
F2. Performance: lexicalJaccard runs for every unit x node pair in candidate generation, and sourceUnit/sourceNode now project both charts (SemanticProjection.sourceOrder) on every call, which lexical never reads. My structural shims pay the same cost, but they need the graphs. Given the Native 30s timeouts, the graph in UnitContent/TargetContent should become a lazy val, or lexical should get a graph-free projection. This touches content.scala, so I'll take it unless you want it.
